name: Minneapolis–Saint Paul
operatingHours: METRO Blue and Green Line light rail runs ~4:00 AM–1:00 AM (Blue Line from ~3:30 AM), every ~10–15 min by day and ~20–30 min late evening. No overnight trains, except that the two airport stations (Terminal 1 and Terminal 2) are linked 24 hours, by train or a free overnight shuttle.
fareInfo: $2 per ride at any time (since 2025), valid 2.5 hours with unlimited transfers to buses and the other line; $1 for youth, seniors (65+) and Medicare card holders. Rides within the downtown Minneapolis or downtown Saint Paul zones cost 50¢. All-Day Pass $4 (to 2:00 AM), 7-day pass $20. Buy at station machines, in the Metro Transit app or with a Go-To card before boarding (proof-of-payment, fines enforced); tap-to-pay with bank cards is not yet live (planned ~2027). The Blue Line ride between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 is free.

sights.name: Minnehaha Park & Falls
sights.note: A leafy riverside park where Minnehaha Creek plunges 16 m over a limestone ledge into a glen, with trails down to the Mississippi; a short walk from 50th Street/Minnehaha Park on the Blue Line. Free.

sights.name: Minneapolis Institute of Art
sights.note: A vast, free encyclopedic museum spanning Rembrandt, Van Gogh, Chinese jades, period rooms and a strong Prairie School collection.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, till 9:00 PM Thu, closed Mon

sights.name: Mill City Museum
sights.note: Built into the burned-out ruins of what was once the world's largest flour mill, with an elevator ride through the mill's history and a rooftop view over St. Anthony Falls. Tickets sold on site only.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed some weekdays (check mnhs.org/millcity)

sights.name: Target Field
sights.note: The Minnesota Twins' downtown ballpark, with skyline views from the upper deck; behind-the-scenes tours run on non-game days.
sights.hours: Twins home games Apr–Sep; ballpark tours on select days year-round

sights.name: Minneapolis Sculpture Garden
sights.note: The Walker Art Center's free outdoor garden of some 60 works, home of Oldenburg and van Bruggen's giant Spoonbridge and Cherry.

sights.name: Guthrie Theater
sights.note: Jean Nouvel's dark-blue riverside theatre; even without a show ticket you can walk out onto its cantilevered Endless Bridge for a free view of the river and Stone Arch Bridge.
sights.hours: Lobbies and Endless Bridge open ~8:00 AM–8:00 PM (later on show nights)

sights.name: American Swedish Institute
sights.note: A turreted 1908 limestone mansion with carved woodwork and tile stoves, joined to a modern wing for Nordic exhibitions and a well-loved Swedish café.

sights.name: Foshay Tower Museum & Observation Deck
sights.note: The 1929 Art Deco obelisk modelled on the Washington Monument, now the W hotel; a small museum leads to an open-air deck on the 30th floor with downtown views. $20, tickets at the hotel's welcome desk.

sights.name: Chain of Lakes (Bde Maka Ska & Lake Harriet)
sights.note: A string of city lakes joined by shoreline paths for walking, cycling and summer paddling; the pin marks the Bde Maka Ska pavilion, with Lake Harriet's bandshell and Lake of the Isles' mansions a stroll away.
sights.hours: Shoreline paths open 6:00 AM–10:00 PM daily; free

sights.name: The Basilica of Saint Mary
sights.note: America's first basilica, a Beaux-Arts landmark with a soaring copper dome and stained glass, next to Loring Park at the edge of downtown.
sights.hours: Open daily for visits outside Mass, ~7:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: The Museum of Russian Art
sights.note: A small museum in a converted Spanish-revival church in south Minneapolis, showing Soviet-era and earlier Russian painting, icons and decorative arts.

sights.name: Stone Arch Bridge
sights.note: A curving 1883 granite railway bridge, now for walkers and cyclists only, with the best views of St. Anthony Falls and the downtown skyline; reopened in 2025 after restoration.

sights.name: Cathedral of Saint Paul
sights.note: A colossal domed cathedral on the hilltop above downtown Saint Paul, modelled on St. Peter's in Rome and lined with marble and glowing rose windows.
sights.hours: Open daily, ~7:00 AM–6:00 PM (shorter around weekend Masses)

sights.name: Como Park Zoo & Conservatory
sights.note: A free zoo with polar bears, gorillas and big cats beside a glass Victorian conservatory and Japanese garden in Saint Paul's Como Park.
sights.hours: Zoo 10:00 AM–4:00 PM daily (to 6:00 PM May–Labor Day); conservatory Tue–Sun

sights.name: Science Museum of Minnesota
sights.note: A hands-on science museum on the Mississippi bluff in Saint Paul, with dinosaur skeletons, a human-body gallery and a domed Omnitheater.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, till 8:00 PM Fri–Sat, closed Mon

sights.name: James J. Hill House
sights.note: The red-sandstone 1891 mansion of the 'Empire Builder' railroad baron, seen on guided tours; it anchors a walk along Summit Avenue's Victorian mansions.
sights.hours: Guided tours Thu–Sun 10:00 AM–4:00 PM (Jan–Nov); holiday tours from 28 Nov

sights.name: Minnesota State Capitol
sights.note: Cass Gilbert's white-marble capitol with a gilded quadriga and one of the world's largest unsupported marble domes; free guided tours.
sights.hours: ~8:30 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Fri, 10:00 AM–3:00 PM Sat, 1:00–5:00 PM Sun

sights.name: Midtown Global Market
sights.note: A food hall in a restored Sears building on Lake Street, packed with Somali, Mexican, Vietnamese and Scandinavian stalls; local-flavor pick.

railStations.name: Saint Paul Union Depot
railStations.note: Restored 1926 Beaux-Arts depot in Lowertown, Saint Paul: Amtrak's Empire Builder (Chicago–Seattle/Portland) and the Borealis to Milwaukee and Chicago stop here. The Green Line's Union Depot terminus is at the front door, ~45 min to downtown Minneapolis.
railStations.hours: Station open ~6:00 AM–11:00 PM daily (later for delayed Amtrak trains). Green Line runs ~4:30 AM–midnight.

airports.name: Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport
airports.transitNote: The METRO Blue Line (shown on map) stops at both Terminal 1 (via the tram level under the parking ramps) and Terminal 2, reaching downtown Minneapolis (Nicollet Mall) in ~25 min for $2. For Saint Paul, change to the Green Line downtown (~1 hr total) or take a taxi (~20 min).
airports.hours: Blue Line: first ~4:00 AM, last ~12:30 AM toward downtown. Terminal 1–2 link runs 24 hours (free overnight shuttle).
